intent.subject: Captain Shalabi (C-01) in three-quarter close-up, his moonlit face turned toward Mahmoud off to the side.
intent.action: Taking in the intercepted-signal warning, his eyes harden and he gives a short, low, absolute order to shut down the radio.
intent.setting: LOC-0003, in the Tina Plain marsh during the company’s night movement.

research.claim: The company is shown beginning its march through the Tina Plain/marsh after the early helicopter drop.
research.note: Follows production decision D-1 to use the Egyptian account of the early Tina Plain drop and long march; the landing location and march distance remain disputed and require the episode end-card source note.

research.claim: The precise setting of this first-march moment as full night is not explicitly established in the ledger.
research.note: H-05 and H-08 support the drop and march, but do not establish this beat's exact time of night.

research.claim: Composite Corporal Mahmoud sends/receives and decodes the coded radio traffic, warns Shalabi that the signal was intercepted, worries about losing contact with command, and switches off the set.
research.note: Mahmoud is a composite character. His actions dramatize the sourced intercepted-signal and radio-silence event without assigning it to a documented real individual.

research.claim: Captain Hamdi Shalabi orders radio silence after the intercepted-signal warning.
research.note: The coded warning and Shalabi's radio-silence order are stated by the primary Egyptian account; the marked dialogue is a permitted dramatized paraphrase.

research.claim: Shalabi taps the switched-off radio and draws a finger across his lips to communicate the sourced radio-silence order; the file passes the silent signal back man to man.
research.note: Permitted staging under P-01: the gestures visually show the sourced radio-silence order and add no new event or outcome.

research.claim: Composite Sergeant Sayed hears the silence order and asks whether the enemy is waiting for them.
research.note: Sayed is a composite character; the question is fictional character dialogue and does not credit him with a documented act.

research.claim: Shalabi uses his compass, changes the file's bearing, and directs the company toward an unexpected approach after the interception warning.
research.note: The route-change dialogue is an approved paraphrase of the source treatment that the enemy did not expect anyone to come from that direction. The compass and turning-file business are permitted P-01 staging.

research.claim: The Soviet-pattern manpack radio, whip antenna, handset placement, and use of red light are presented as period equipment/detail.
research.note: The ledger documents radio traffic and silence, but does not source this specific radio model/configuration or red-light procedure.

flags.detail: The beat fixes the company's first steps into the marsh at night, but the ledger does not establish the exact time for this moment.
The specific Soviet-pattern manpack radio configuration, whip antenna, handset placement, and red-light decoding procedure are not sourced in the ledger.

direction.coverage: Hold a three-quarter close-up on Shalabi, with Mahmoud kept as a soft off-axis presence.
direction.blocking: Shalabi stays still in the marsh column, turning only his gaze toward Mahmoud before issuing the order.
direction.performance_note: Let the warning register in a hardening stare; deliver the shutdown command low, clipped, and unquestionable.
direction.pacing: A brief listening beat, then an immediate decisive command.
direction.tone_ref: Restrained historical war realism—moonlit tension, disciplined command, no melodrama.

wardrobe.additions: Egyptian captain's rank: exactly three small gold five-pointed stars in a row on each plain khaki shoulder strap, plain khaki collar with no collar tabs or badges, compass on a lanyard (PRP-0008)
visible_details: Bare-headed short black hair, damp and flattened by night marsh humidity.
Sand-khaki cotton field jacket in three-quarter close-up, with the plain khaki collar visible; no collar tabs, chest eagle badge, or modern insignia.
Exactly three small gold five-pointed captain’s stars in a row on the shoulder strap nearest camera; the far strap may remain out of view at this framing.
Soviet-pattern khaki canvas chest-rig strap and simple plain metal buckle may enter the lower frame; no modern tactical vest.
Compass on its lanyard may sit at the lower chest edge if framed, dull and wet rather than prominent.
WEAR_MUD reads as wet dark splashes and brine sheen across the jacket front, shoulder, and rolled forearm; soaked mud-darkened trousers are off-frame in this close-up.
wardrobe.notes: Continuity: retains the cold night-marsh wetness from the preceding radio close-up, but Shalabi is keyed by moonlight rather than Mahmoud’s red-filtered torch; keep gold rank stars subdued, not shiny.

makeup.skin_state: Medium-olive face damp with cold exertion, a restrained moonlit sheen across the forehead, nose bridge, cheekbones and upper lip; fine dark mud specks and brine streaking at the lower cheeks, jaw and neck, with a few tiny pale salt traces caught in the eyebrows. No blood or visible wounds.
makeup.hair_state: Bare-headed short black hair remains neatly side-parted but damp and slightly flattened at the temples; straight black eyebrows damp and lightly salt-flecked. Thin handlebar mustache is wet but intact, with its upturned ends preserved.
makeup.notes: Keep his long narrow face, hollow cheeks, pointed chin, thin lips and intense narrow dark-brown eyes fully readable in three-quarter moonlight. Fatigue is controlled: slight under-eye shadow and tightened jaw, not exhaustion or panic.

dressing: thin white salt crust over black mud
small shallow brine sheets with dim moon reflections
low sparse salt-marsh vegetation at the frame edge
subtle wet mud flecks and brine sheen on the captain's lower uniform
set.set_state: Cold, featureless Tina Plain marsh at night; shallow mid-shin brine and broken salt crust remain undisturbed in the tight frame.
set.notes: Keep PRP-0008 held low at the captain's chest or just below frame, with no readable map markings visible; maintain a clean moonlit facial plane and only a minimal dark marsh background.

camera.light: Moonlight and starlight only: a soft, cool blue-black key rakes across Shalabi’s turned face from the off-axis Mahmoud side, leaving the far cheek in controlled shadow and a faint cold rim on hair and shoulder; no red radio glow or artificial fill reaches him. Keep the marsh behind him as soft, near-black salt-and-brine texture.
camera.exposure_note: Expose low for a true moonlit night while holding readable catchlight-free eyes, mouth, lips, and khaki facial detail; retain deep shadows without crushing his speaking mouth or three gold captain’s shoulder stars if the strap edges into frame.
camera.framing_note: Generate 16:9 for a 2.39:1 center-band crop: retain Shalabi’s eyes, full lip-sync mouth, and three-quarter facial silhouette within the middle 75% height, with his eyeline held off-axis toward the unseen Mahmoud; keep all off-axis presence fully out of frame.

action.choreography: Shalabi holds still in the shallow marsh column, listens toward the off-axis Mahmoud, then delivers a low, clipped, absolute order to shut down the radio. Keep the performance contained to eye focus, facial tightening, and clearly lip-synced speech.
action.movement: No body movement or combat action; only a minute off-axis gaze set and controlled mouth movement in three-quarter close-up.
beats: Still listening beat toward off-axis Mahmoud.
Eyes fix and harden without turning toward camera.
He speaks the shutdown order low and unmistakably.
He holds the command stare after speaking.
